name: Singapore
tagline: A garden city of hawker feasts, Supertrees and skyline swims
description:
Singapore squeezes the energy of a global city into an island you can cross by train in about an hour, then wraps it all in greenery. Futuristic Supertrees and a rooftop infinity pool share the skyline with colonial shophouses, Hindu temples, Malay mosques and Chinese clan halls, and each neighborhood carries its own flavors and festivals.

Flavor is the point. Hawker centers, open-air food courts whose culture is now recognized by UNESCO, serve Michelin-noted chicken rice, laksa and char kway teow for a few dollars, while a seat at a celebrated tasting-menu counter can cost more than your flight. Most visitors end up happily doing both, sometimes on the same day.

It is also one of the easiest places in Asia to travel: English is spoken everywhere, the MRT is spotless, tap water is safe to drink and the rules are famously strict, from no eating on trains to no chewing gum for sale. It is hot and humid year-round with sudden tropical storms, so save outdoor sights for mornings and evenings and duck into air-conditioned museums at midday.

safety.notes: One of the safest cities in the world, with very low street crime at any hour. Take the laws seriously: littering, jaywalking and drug offenses carry heavy penalties, and vaping is illegal.

tipping: Tipping isn't expected; most restaurants add a 10% service charge plus 9% GST, and hawker stalls never expect a tip.
gettingAround: The MRT and buses cover the whole island and accept contactless bank cards and phones directly at the gates. Grab and metered taxis are reasonably priced for late nights.
tips: At hawker centers, locals 'chope' (reserve) a table by leaving a packet of tissues on it; never move someone's tissues, and bring your own pack.
Stalls that make just one dish are usually the best; follow the longest queue of office workers at lunchtime and don't be put off by a 15-minute wait.
Catch the free Garden Rhapsody light show under the Supertrees at 19:45 or 20:45, then walk over for Marina Bay's free Spectra water show.
Jewel at Changi Airport, with its indoor waterfall, is free to visit and open late, so arrive early for your flight or stop by on arrival day.
Carry a compact umbrella; afternoon thunderstorms are frequent, especially November to January, but covered walkways link most MRT stations to nearby sights.
Order coffee like a local: 'kopi' comes with condensed milk, 'kopi-O' is black with sugar, 'kopi-C' uses evaporated milk and 'kosong' means no sugar.
etiquette: Eating and drinking, even water, are banned on the MRT and buses, and fines apply.
Remove your shoes before entering mosques and Hindu temples and cover shoulders and knees; the Sultan Mosque lends robes at the door.
Return your tray and crockery after eating at hawker centers; it is required by law, with separate return points for halal and non-halal dishes.
Queue patiently and never cut in; Singaporeans take queues, and their place in them, very seriously.

phrases.pronunciation: AH-pah KAH-bar (Malay 'how are you?', used as a friendly hello)
TOH-long (Malay; Singlish just adds 'can?' as in 'Help me, can?')
KAN (Singlish all-purpose yes; 'can lah' for extra certainty)
KAN-not (Singlish firm no, as in 'Cannot lah, sold out already')
TAHN-dahs dee MAH-nah (Malay; Singlish: 'Toilet where ah?')
BOSS, kan BILL (Singlish; 'boss' works for any waiter or stall owner)

neighborhoods.name: Chinatown
neighborhoods.blurb: Temple-studded shophouse streets with hawker centers, traditional medicine halls and cocktail bars along Club Street and Keong Saik Road.

neighborhoods.name: Kampong Glam
neighborhoods.blurb: The historic Malay-Arab quarter around the Sultan Mosque, with Haji Lane's murals and boutiques, perfume shops and Middle Eastern cafés.

neighborhoods.name: Little India
neighborhoods.blurb: A riot of color, jasmine garlands and spice shops centered on Serangoon Road, with superb South Indian food and bargain shopping.

neighborhoods.name: Tiong Bahru
neighborhoods.blurb: One of Singapore's oldest public housing estates, with 1930s Art Deco flats, independent bookshops, bakeries and a beloved wet market.

neighborhoods.name: Katong-Joo Chiat
neighborhoods.blurb: Pastel Peranakan terrace houses, laksa shops and heritage bakeries in a laid-back east-coast district.

dishes.name: Hainanese chicken rice
dishes.description: Silky poached chicken on rice cooked in chicken stock, ginger and pandan, with chili-garlic sauce and dark soy; the unofficial national dish.

dishes.name: Laksa
dishes.description: Katong-style curry laksa: thick rice noodles cut short in a coconut and dried-shrimp broth with cockles and fish cake, eaten with just a spoon.

dishes.name: Chili crab
dishes.description: Mud crab wok-tossed in a sweet, tangy tomato-chili gravy thickened with egg; mop up every drop with fried mantou buns.

dishes.name: Kaya toast
dishes.description: Charcoal-toasted bread sandwiching cold butter and coconut-pandan jam, dipped into soft-boiled eggs seasoned with soy and white pepper.

dishes.name: Char kway teow
dishes.description: Flat rice noodles fried over a roaring flame with cockles, Chinese sausage, bean sprouts and sweet dark soy for smoky wok hei.

events.name: Chinese New Year
events.description: Chinatown's streets glow with lanterns and festive bazaars, and the Chingay street parade brings floats and performers to the city a couple of weeks later; the date shifts between late January and February.

events.name: National Day
events.description: On August 9 Singapore celebrates independence with a spectacular parade, fighter-jet flypasts and fireworks over Marina Bay; the July rehearsals are almost as good.

events.name: Mid-Autumn Festival
events.description: Lantern displays light up Chinatown and Gardens by the Bay while bakeries sell mooncakes filled with lotus paste, salted egg yolk and ever more creative flavors.

events.name: Singapore Grand Prix
events.description: Formula 1's original night race roars through the streets around Marina Bay, with concerts and parties across the city all weekend; some years it falls in late September.

attractions.name: Gardens by the Bay
attractions.description: Giant steel Supertrees draped in ferns and orchids tower over this waterfront garden, linked by an aerial walkway. Inside the two chilled conservatories, the Cloud Forest's misty mountain and plunging indoor waterfall steal the show, and a free light show plays under the Supertrees every evening.
attractions.bookingTip: Book conservatory tickets online for a late-afternoon slot, then stay for the 19:45 Garden Rhapsody show; the outdoor gardens are free.

attractions.name: Marina Bay Sands
attractions.description: Three towers topped by a ship-shaped SkyPark define Singapore's skyline. The famous infinity pool is for hotel guests only, but the observation deck delivers the same 200-meter views across the bay, and the free Spectra light-and-water show plays on the promenade each night.
attractions.bookingTip: Book a sunset slot online, or put the ticket price toward a cocktail at one of the rooftop bars instead.

attractions.name: Singapore Botanic Gardens
attractions.description: Singapore's first UNESCO World Heritage Site is a tropical garden more than 160 years old, with rainforest trails, swan lakes and lawns where locals picnic to free weekend concerts. Don't miss the National Orchid Garden, where more than a thousand species and countless hybrids bloom, some named after visiting celebrities and heads of state.
attractions.bookingTip: The main gardens are free; the National Orchid Garden costs about $12 and is best before 10:00, while it is still cool.

attractions.name: Chinatown
attractions.description: Shophouse lanes pack in the grand Buddha Tooth Relic Temple, the ornate Hindu Sri Mariamman Temple and a sprawling hawker center where award-winning stalls sell soy-sauce chicken for a few dollars. After dark, Keong Saik Road and Club Street fill with cocktail bars.
attractions.bookingTip: Hit the Chinatown Complex hawker center at lunch before stalls sell out, and visit the temple's rooftop garden in the late afternoon.

attractions.name: Sultan Mosque
attractions.description: The golden domes of one of Singapore's most important mosques anchor the Kampong Glam quarter; look for the band of glass-bottle ends at the base of the domes, donated by poorer worshippers. Volunteers welcome visitors outside prayer times and lend robes for modest dress.
attractions.bookingTip: Avoid Friday midday prayers, and come during Ramadan evenings for the bazaar food stalls around the mosque.

attractions.name: Little India
attractions.description: Jasmine garlands, spice-scented shops and gold jewelers line Serangoon Road, where the ornate Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple hums with prayer. Grab a banana-leaf curry lunch, then browse the Tekka Centre's wet market and fabric stalls.
attractions.bookingTip: Weekday mornings are best for the Tekka Centre market; Sunday evenings get extremely crowded.

attractions.name: Singapore Zoo
attractions.description: Widely rated among the world's best, this 'open' zoo uses moats and streams instead of cages across a rainforest setting on the edge of a reservoir. Book breakfast near the orangutans, then pair it with the Night Safari next door for a full day and evening.
attractions.bookingTip: Buy tickets online for a discount, and pack a poncho for the sudden afternoon downpours.

attractions.name: National Gallery Singapore
attractions.description: Two colonial landmarks, the former Supreme Court and City Hall, are joined beneath a golden canopy to house the world's largest public collection of modern Southeast Asian art. The rooftop garden has one of the best views over the Padang and Marina Bay.
attractions.bookingTip: Buy tickets online, and don't skip the rooftop garden, which is free to visit even without a gallery ticket.

attractions.name: Universal Studios Singapore
attractions.description: Southeast Asia's first Universal park squeezes a Transformers dark ride, dueling Battlestar Galactica coasters and a Jurassic Park river raft into a compact site on Sentosa, alongside the newer Minion Land. Weekdays outside school holidays mean far shorter queues.
attractions.bookingTip: Buy tickets online at least a day ahead and add an Express pass on weekends and during school holidays.

attractions.name: Lau Pa Sat
attractions.description: A Victorian cast-iron market hall in the middle of the financial district, now a hawker center serving everything from prawn noodles to Indian rojak. In the evening the street alongside closes to traffic and becomes 'Satay Street', with smoky grills and outdoor tables.
attractions.hours: Open 24 hours; Satay Street from 19:00 nightly
attractions.bookingTip: Satay is sold in bundles of ten, so order a mix of chicken, mutton and prawn and share it with a jug of cold beer.

hotels.name: Straits Pearl Tower
hotels.description: A glass tower on the bay with a 50-meter rooftop lap pool facing the Supertrees and an orchid-filled atrium lobby. Butlers will pack your beach bag for Sentosa, and the Peranakan afternoon tea has a devoted local following.

hotels.name: The Five-Foot Way Hotel
hotels.description: A row of 1920s shophouses restored with their original tiles, timber shutters and air wells, now 32 rooms above a cocktail bar. Step out the door straight into Chinatown's hawker and bar scene.

hotels.name: Jasmine Garland Hostel
hotels.description: Clean, air-conditioned capsule pods with lockers and reading lights, plus a rooftop kitchen overlooking Little India. Breakfast of kaya toast and kopi is free, and the MRT is two minutes' walk away.

hotels.name: Songket House
hotels.description: Rooms riff on Malay songket weaving with jewel-toned textiles and brass lamps, and the rooftop looks straight at the Sultan Mosque's golden dome. Haji Lane's cafés and boutiques are just around the corner.
highlights: Around the corner from Haji Lane

hotels.name: Palawan Breeze Resort
hotels.description: A low-rise family resort on Sentosa with a lazy river, kids' club and lagoon pool, a short island tram ride from Universal Studios. Evenings bring beach barbecues and outdoor movie screenings.

hotels.name: Tanglin Garden Residences
hotels.description: Serviced apartments with full kitchens and balconies on a quiet street near the Botanic Gardens' Tanglin Gate, ten minutes' walk from Orchard Road. Twice-weekly housekeeping and a lap pool make longer stays easy.

restaurants.name: Bara Api Satay
restaurants.description: One of the busiest grills on Satay Street, fanning skewers of lemongrass-marinated chicken, mutton and prawn over charcoal and serving them with a pineapple-laced peanut sauce. Order by the ten and grab an outdoor table.
restaurants.signatureDish: Mixed satay with ketupat rice cakes

restaurants.name: Pandan Leaf Chicken Rice
restaurants.description: A hawker stall with a queue of office workers every lunchtime for its silky poached chicken, pandan-scented rice and fierce house chili. It sells out by 14:00 most days, so go early.

restaurants.name: Tembusu Kopi House
restaurants.description: An old-school coffee shop revived near the gardens' Tanglin Gate, where coffee is pulled through cloth socks and the kaya jam is cooked daily from coconut milk and pandan. The perfect stop after an early garden walk.
restaurants.signatureDish: Kaya toast set with soft-boiled eggs and kopi

restaurants.name: Kembang Api
restaurants.description: Candlelit tasting menus reinterpret Peranakan family recipes with luxury produce, from wagyu rendang to buah keluak black-nut ice cream, on the top floor of a colonial building facing the Padang. Book three weeks ahead for the counter overlooking the open kitchen.

restaurants.name: Ketam Merah Seafood
restaurants.description: An open-sided seafood restaurant by the water, known for Sri Lankan mud crabs in two styles: sweet-sour chili and fiery black pepper. Don't skip the fried mantou buns for mopping up the sauce.

restaurants.name: Kolam Kitchen
restaurants.description: Rice, three vegetables, papadum and endless refills of dal and curry served on a banana leaf, with a legendary fish-head curry for groups. Eat with your right hand like the regulars and finish with a frothy pulled tea.

restaurants.name: Kedai Minyak Sapi
restaurants.description: An old-style Muslim eatery facing the mosque, famous for crisp murtabak folded around spiced mutton and egg and served with a fish curry dip. Wash it down with a glass of sweet ginger tea.

restaurants.name: Coast & Crust Pizzeria
restaurants.description: A beachfront wood-fired pizzeria a short walk from the theme park, turning out blistered Neapolitan pies, simple kids' pastas and gelato. Grab a table on the sand at sunset.

experiences.name: Hawker Heroes Food Trail
experiences.description: A food-writer guide leads you through two hawker centers and a heritage coffee shop, ordering a dozen dishes from chicken rice to rojak and explaining how each community shaped Singapore's plate. You'll also learn to order kopi like a local.

experiences.name: Twilight Bumboat Heritage Cruise
experiences.description: Chug along the Singapore River aboard a wooden bumboat while a storyteller recounts the laborers, traders and merchants who built the quays, then glide onto Marina Bay in time for the Spectra light show.

experiences.name: Little India Spice Market & Curry Class
experiences.description: Shop for spices, curry leaves and fresh coconut at Tekka Centre with a home cook, then learn to grind masalas and cook a South Indian feast of fish curry, dal and chapati in her public-housing flat kitchen.

experiences.name: Night Safari & Rainforest Explorer
experiences.description: Transfer at dusk to the Mandai wildlife parks for a guided walk along the Night Safari's leopard and fishing-cat trails and a reserved tram ride through the forest. Dinner of Malay favorites overlooking the trees is included.
